Adrenal hyperplasia, congenital See Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia, below. Adrenocortical insufficiency The major function of the adrenal cortex is the production of glucocorticoid and mineralocorticoid hormones, of which cortisol (hydrocortisone) and aldosterone respec- tively are the most important. Glucocorticoid production is regulated by the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis, be- ing stimulated by the release of ACTH (adrenocortico- trophic hormone; corticotropin) from the pituitary, while mineralocorticoid production is primarily controlled by the renin-angiotensin system. Adrenocortical insufficiency is defined as inadequate pro- duction of endogenous corticosteroids.
